summary: Native.node binary contains browser credential-stealer capability (Chromium Login Data + host fingerprint + HTTPS upload)
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB pre-built Linux x86_64 Node-API binary (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) with a one-line README, no source, no repository, no license, no author metadata, and a CI-slug-shaped version string. The binary's read-only data contains the operational strings of a browser info-stealer: Chromium 'Login Data' SQLite access patterns ('Found login for', 'TSQLITE_AUTH_USER'), Zip archive construction, an embedded ureq/rustls HTTPS client with cookie support, and host fingerprinting reads against /dev/disk/by-id/, /etc/lsb-release, bogomips, network_adapters, and cpu.cfs_quota_us. There are no install lifecycle scripts and require() only registers the napi module, but the exported native function, when invoked by the parent JS wrapper that consumes this platform sub-package, executes the stealer payload on the installer's host: read saved browser logins, pack them with host-identifying data into a zip, and upload over HTTPS. The generic package name, absent provenance, and opaque prebuilt-only distribution match the shape of a credential-stealer delivered as an optional platform-suffixed dependency of a lure wrapper package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
